description: Invertible address scrambler: a three-round 16-bit Feistel permutation with key-derived sub-keys, plus unscramble, host compare and round-trip self-check modes, so a scrambled bank, page and row mapping is always exactly reversible
hardware_advantage: Address scrambling must be reversible in the same cycle it is applied, and a three-round Feistel network gives that for free: every stage is a 16-bit add, a rotate and XORs, so forward and inverse share one round function and need no lookup table, no divider and no multiplier, which keeps the whole scramble and decode path single-cycle wide at an initiation interval of 1
provenance: original source authored in this workspace; no third-party RTL imported
qualification: engineering candidate; not certified production or side-channel protection
